text: {"frames":["The portrait of the old miller's wife in the corridor has turned her head toward the stairs since last night. Imogen, the old lock keeper, says the clock beside her never ran slow before the Tower woke. Its hands have crept round in the dark, and the brass pendulum hangs still behind the glass. Before the stairs can be climbed, the lock gates must open at the right moment, so the whole floor is waiting on it. What time does the clock in the picture show?","The water in the lock rose and fell all night, as if the canal were breathing in its sleep. Fenna, the learned owl from the mill, sat on the gate and would not say a word until she knew the hour. The bell in the tower had been silent since the thread tangled, so only the clock in the picture on the wall could tell. The barge with the blue lantern is waiting below, and the owl will only fly if the hour is right. What time does the clock in the picture show?","The stairs went up one step further than the plan allowed, and at the top there was a floor nobody had drawn. A small door stood open, with a note pinned to it that read, Please come before the hour is over. Briony, the stork who talks, flapped down beside you and tapped the clock in the picture by the door with her beak. She said the bells of the town were ringing for the market, and the door would close when the hands reached the right place. What time does the clock in the picture show?","The canal ran backwards in the night, and this morning the herring boats lay on the wrong side of the bridge. A cheese maker found his wheel of cheese sitting in the window of a house that is not his. On the wall of the market hall hangs the clock in the picture, and everyone in Misty Ford is standing under it. The eel-seller says the canal will turn back once the clock shows the time it showed when the water first moved. What time does the clock in the picture show?","A blue light moved through the mill at night, and in the morning a clog was found in the cellar with a clock painted on its sole. The miller's apprentice claims it is the same clock as the one in the picture on the dyke house wall. Somebody has been counting clogs at night, and the count will not come right until the hour is found. The waffle seller has promised the apprentice a warm waffle if the hour is named before the ice on the canal melts. What time does the clock in the picture show?"]}
